author: Ernest Thompson Seton
title: Wild Animals at Home
edition: Garden City, New York: Doubleday, Page & Company, 1923; dated title page, copyright 1913 by Ernest Thompson Seton. Ornamental star dividers are omitted. Prose soft line-wraps are joined; paragraph boundaries, wording, punctuation, and transcription emphasis markers remain. Illustration placeholders, captions, and ornamental star dividers are excluded, without omitting narrative text. The library text holds the author’s foreword, all twelve chapters with their section titles and footnotes, and the 1912 species list; the title, contents and plate list pages, the repeated half-titles and the transcriber’s notes are excluded. Chapter numbers are joined with their titles as headings.

rights.basis: The 1923 English edition was published before 1931 and its US copyright term has expired as of 2026. Project Gutenberg explicitly marks the transcription public domain in the USA. Only the original literary text is reproduced, not later editorial matter or illustrations.

acquisition.method: Project Gutenberg plain text (eBook 27887, UTF-8) from the PG mirror. Kept Seton’s Foreword and signature, Chapters I–XII with their section titles, his three footnotes as transcribed ([A]–[C] calls, “[Footnote …]” paragraphs after each chapter’s FOOTNOTES: label, which is a paragraph) and the closing list of species found in the Park in 1912; removed the PG header and footer, title and copyright pages, contents, list of half-tone plates, the starred half-title pages that repeat each chapter title, [Illustration] placeholders and plate captions, ornamental star dividers and the transcriber’s notes. Blank-line separated paragraphs were joined into single-spaced prose (each species entry with its indented note is one paragraph); the indented list of four bats keeps its lines. Chapter numbers are joined with their titles as headings; capitalised section titles are subheadings. Converted by a scratch Node script; every nightly reading was located exactly.
